newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weak yen forces Japan to postpone grain buying.
newsitem.headline: Weak yen forces Japan to postpone grain buying.

text.p: The yen's steep fall against the dollar is forcing Japan's Food Agency to postpone some of its planned purchases of wheat and barley, agency sources said on Thursday.
The Food Agency said earlier on Thursday that it had bought 80,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 20,000 of Canadian barley and 20,000 of Australian barley at its weekly tender.
But it originally planned to buy another 20,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat, 37,000 tonnes of Australian wheat and 20,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, the sources said.
"There's a growing gap between the Food Agency and trade houses on import prices, mainly because of the weak yen," a source said.
The Food Agency, the grain trading arm of the Agriculture Ministry, was forced to carry out the import tender twice because offer prices from local trade houses were not low enough, the sources said.
